headline: Across 12 backtests — four universes at three holding periods, two statistics each — none showed a relationship between a name's rank and its subsequent return that survives correcting for having run them all. 1 of the 24 individual tests cleared the conventional 5% cutoff before correction, against 1.2 expected from chance alone at that many tests — which is why the correction is applied rather than the best result quoted. The most sensitive of them could only have detected a mean information coefficient of about 0.08, and a useful one in this field is nearer 0.03 — so this is 'no edge large enough to see here', not 'no edge'.

dow30:21.verdict: No significant relationship between rank and subsequent return in this sample. The top fifth beat the bottom by -0.98% per period on average, which is not distinguishable from zero (t = -1.49, p = 0.142); the mean information coefficient is -0.036. On this evidence the composite orders the universe without demonstrably predicting it. This test could only have detected a mean information coefficient of about 0.088 or larger, so a real but modest edge would be invisible in a sample this size — 'not found' is not 'not there'.
caveats: Survivorship: the universe is today's constituents, so every name tested is one that survived and is still a member. This biases the result upward and cannot be corrected without point-in-time membership data.
No trading costs, spread, market impact or tax are deducted.
71 non-overlapping periods is a small sample; a t-statistic on it is a weak instrument.
One history, one market regime. Not a distribution of outcomes.
